title: SDK auth patterns: ephemeral tokens, SSO refresh flows, rotation and local secret guidance
creator: Jordan Liu
description:
Problem: Our SDKs (Python/TS/Go) currently expose multiple ad-hoc patterns for credentials that create confusion for users and surface security risk: long-lived API keys embedded in source, unclear rotation guidance, fragile streaming auth behavior (stale headers during multi-minute streams), and insufficient examples for enterprise SSO token flows.

Goal: Produce a consolidated SDK-level guidance and ergonomic helpers that: (1) recommend secure defaults for API key usage, (2) provide first-class helpers for short-lived/ephemeral credentials and rotation automation, (3) document and implement SSO token refresh workflows (OIDC / SAML -> Redwood tokens) across languages, and (4) include developer ergonomics for local dev (CLI token helper + OS keychain examples) and for streaming sessions where tokens may need dynamic refresh.

Scope: Deliverables across languages:
- High-level guidance doc (CONFLUENCE + SDK README snippets) describing patterns and tradeoffs.
- SDK helper APIs: credential providers and refresh hooks in Python/TS/Go. These should support: env var fallback, file-based credentials, OS keychains (macOS/Windows/Linux), and an ephemeral provider that exchanges an identity token for a short-lived Redwood token.
- Streaming example and helper that transparently re-auths mid-stream without data corruption or reconnection where possible; fallbacks documented.
- Rotation automation recipe (GitHub Actions + webhook) for rotating API keys and verifying SDK reconnect behavior.
- End-to-end examples: repo with sample apps (one each in Python/TS/Go) demonstrating local dev, CI secrets, and enterprise SSO flow.

Non-goals: Rewriting auth server or changing existing token formats. Large infra changes to the auth backend are out of scope for this ticket; this work focuses on SDK surface and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative Confluence doc published: 'SDK Auth Patterns - ephemeral tokens, SSO refresh, rotation' with diagrams and examples.

Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a consistent CredentialProvider interface and at least two built-in providers: EnvOrFileProvider and EphemeralExchangeProvider (which calls a configured token-exchange endpoint).

Streaming helper implemented that supports header refresh during streaming for Python and TypeScript SDKs; documented behavior and graceful fallback for servers that don’t support mid-stream renegotiation.
Local dev CLI helper (redwood-auth-cli) published in samples that can mint short-lived tokens and optionally store them in OS keychain; example usage in README for all three languages.
Rotation playbook (GitHub Actions + verification script) in sample repo that demonstrates rotating keys and auto-validating SDK reconnection within 5 minutes.
Security review completed and signoff recorded (security_review_required=true).
Unit + integration tests covering token refresh, 401 handling and retry backoff added to SDK test suites.
At least two customer-facing sample apps updated (one PLG quickstart and one enterprise example) demonstrating recommended flows.
